problems: Commonwealth of England: Cliopatria row is 1645-1661 but the state is 19 May 1649 - May 1660; the 1645-1648 Parliament-side England and Wales shape has no owner unless the kingdom-of-england dossier covers it (its Cliopatria shapes for 1645-1652 are only the royalist remnant). Decide: start the Commonwealth in 1645 or assign 1642-1649 to the England dossier.

Kingdom of Scotland is extended from Cliopatria's 1294-1608 to 1294-May 1707 (page infobox 843-1707) with a new 1609-1706 keyframe; Cliopatria draws Scotland inside its Kingdom of England row in 1609-1639, 1662-1706, so Scotland will be doubled unless the England dossier subtracts it. Kingdom of Alba (900-1293) and Scotland are one kingdom and should share a colour.

Earldom of Desmond: Cliopatria's 1333-1351 shape is the Earldom of Ulster's Antrim-Down polygon (wrong); 1422-1458 lies in Tipperary-Kilkenny-Laois (wrong); 1385 and 1395 add Leinster land (adjust). The dossier runs 1329-Nov 1583 (page) against Cliopatria's 1333-1458, with new keyframes 1329-1332 and 1459-1583; all corrections are one four-county union because the pages give no dated change.

Earldom of Ulster is dated 1263-June 1333 (page) against Cliopatria's 1326-1332; its shape was about a third of the page's Antrim-and-Down extent. Overlaps whatever the Lordship of Ireland / England dossiers draw for Antrim and Down.

Isle of Man is 1346-1399 on the pages (Cliopatria 1344-1401); 1400-1401 is covered by neither this row nor the England shapes (which include the island from 1402). Scotland's 1294 and 1314 shapes include the island and are adjusted; matching losses/gains (1313, 1314, 1317, 1333, 1346, Berwick 1318/1482) are expected in the kingdom-of-england dossier.
Scotland's shapes 1552-1608 carry 5-14 grid cells on the Antrim and Down coast with no page support; removed by adjust verdicts.

Page budget: Scotland used its five pages plus the Third English Civil War page (also Commonwealth's) and cites the Isle of Man page (Man's budget); the Commonwealth cites the Irish Confederate Wars and Kingdom of Scotland pages opened for neighbours. Desmond's fifth page (Earl of Ormond) was a disambiguation page. Wikipedia pages were thin on territory throughout; low-confidence events: 2 (Scotland found 1294 and the Hebrides vassal_start, both page-silent).
